subject.title: fix(gateway): stop health monitor from undoing crash-loop give-up

question: After the channel manager exhausts its crash-loop restart budget, should the account remain stopped until explicit operator action, or may the health monitor revive it under a separate bounded policy?
rationale: Current main explicitly tests post-give-up revival, while this PR and the competing candidate make give-up terminal and expose different permanent manager APIs; source correctness cannot select the intended operator-facing availability contract.

options.title: Make give-up terminal
options.body: Select the simplest canonical manager-owned state contract, retain timed-out recovery, and require installed-runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Add bounded revival policy
options.body: Protect active manager backoff but model post-give-up health-monitor revival as a separate explicit and budgeted state.

options.title: Retain current behavior
options.body: Reject both candidates and keep implicit health-monitor revival after manager give-up.

recommendation.title: Make give-up terminal
recommendation.body: Select the simplest canonical manager-owned state contract, retain timed-out recovery, and require installed-runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent recovery hardening and the strongest continuing contribution history make this the best available owner for the lifecycle policy and API decision.
